storyboard.claim: Darrow's clan has no homes, only dwellings cut into the rock.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A wide view of a dark rock cave with a boy slumped on a dirt floor, carved stone walls around him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the township scene after the context about making suffering a religious duty.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the physical living conditions the narration only describes (dirt floors, carved walls).

storyboard.claim: A massive holo cam hangs at the center of the gloomy township.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow points up at a holo cam hanging in the middle of the dim township.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the cave description; introduces the object that becomes the central window.
storyboard.addedInformation: Places the holo cam physically at the center of the community, so the viewer knows where the propaganda comes from.

storyboard.claim: The holo cam is a constant, never-switched-off light in the gloom.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An insert of a faded square box with glowing screens on every side, lighting the dark cave.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes the object introduced in the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: The always-on light shows that the propaganda is constant, not occasional.

storyboard.claim: Through the holo cam, the township sees the face of the ruler Octavia Aloon.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow watches a glowing projection that shows a regal woman's face, the only window to the world.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The cam is established; now the viewer learns what it shows.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the ruler on screen so the face on the cam has an identity.

storyboard.claim: Octavia's face is beautiful and frightening, looking down on starving miners.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A low angle of Darrow's face looking up at the glowing projection of the ruler, who looks down at him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues from the named ruler on the screen.
storyboard.addedInformation: The low camera angle carries the power imbalance: she looks down on them.

storyboard.claim: The crescent scar marks Octavia's elite status.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An insert of the projected face with a crescent scar on the cheekbone, read as a mark of rank.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Zooms in on the ruler's face from the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the scar as a status badge, the rank the narrator says it signals.

storyboard.claim: Octavia flatters the miners as brave pioneers, a flattering story that hides the chain.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow stands on the red dust horizon of Mars, thinking about the praise he hears.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains how the ruler speaks to the miners, after the scar.
storyboard.addedInformation: The Mars horizon shows the pioneer setting the praise refers to.

storyboard.claim: The pioneer story says Earth is dying and humanity is running out of room.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An hourglass beside Darrow under a thin pink sky, the time of Earth running out.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the content of the pioneer myth the previous beat praised.
storyboard.addedInformation: The hourglass shows the urgency the myth uses: time is running out for humanity.

storyboard.claim: The miners' blood and sweat are presented as a down payment for human immortality.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow from blood to a down payment to immortality, with Darrow shown below it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the pioneer story: the mining is framed as a sacrifice.
storyboard.addedInformation: The flow makes the cause-and-effect the narrator describes: suffering buys a promised future.

storyboard.claim: If the miners believe their pain has a cosmic purpose, they see themselves as humanity's savior.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow with a shield, thinking about being the one who protects humankind.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the sacrifice into a self-image the cage depends on.
storyboard.addedInformation: The shield reads as protection, which is what the savior role claims to do.

storyboard.claim: Rebellion is recast as betrayal of the species, not as freedom.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow slumped, his back against the cave wall, under the weight of the accusation.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the savior role: rebelling then looks like treason.
storyboard.addedInformation: Stages the verdict as the internalized guilt, not as a freedom fight; the freedom reading is rejected by the narration.

storyboard.claim: Darrow sees himself as the villain of his own life for resisting.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow in medium shot, a mirror beside him showing his self-image.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the 'traitor' verdict into how Darrow sees himself.
storyboard.addedInformation: The mirror shows the self-judgment: the viewer sees him judging his own reflection.

storyboard.claim: The Sons of Aries are a rebel group, described as terrorists, who want to overthrow the Golds.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The rebel leader speaking in a dim room, with a war icon beside him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the group that the next beats judge.
storyboard.addedInformation: The war icon shows the armed fight they represent; the rest of the group is named by the callout.

storyboard.claim: Darrow despises the rebels, even though a reader would expect him to support them.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow angrily points at the rebel leader in a two-shot.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the group's name and then shows Darrow's contempt for it.
storyboard.addedInformation: The angry point shows the contempt directly, against the reader's expectation.

storyboard.claim: Darrow dismisses the rebels' attacks as pointless noise that delays terraforming.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow with a blank, dismissive face on the Mars horizon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the contempt from the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: The blank face shows indifference to the rebels, which is the attitude the narration describes.

storyboard.claim: Darrow works against his own freedom because the myth has taken over his mind.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow in medium shot, head down, a worried face under the cave lights.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the contempt into the self-defeating result of the myth.
storyboard.addedInformation: The slumped body shows the self-harm the narration describes, without an icon that could be misread.

storyboard.claim: The hosts take a devil's advocate turn and praise Jerro's sharpness.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator speaking to the camera on a plain background.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A turn in the argument: the hosts introduce a counterpoint.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the sharp character whose skepticism the next beats test.

storyboard.claim: The clan is described as tough, cynical, and skeptical.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow thinking, a wary face in the dim township.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes the clan the devil's advocate question is about.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets up the paradox: skeptical people who still believe the myth.

storyboard.claim: The clan is shown a standard propaganda broadcast from a flickering screen.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow with a mask icon beside the glowing screen of the propaganda broadcast.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Raises the question of why skeptical people accept the broadcast.
storyboard.addedInformation: The mask reads as a false public face: the broadcast is a performance, not truth.

storyboard.claim: The clan is not gullible; it is cynical about its own myths.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow with a blank, thinking face: the cynicism is what the viewer sees.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Rejects the easy reading from the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: The strike rejects the 'simpleton' label; the blank cynical face carries the correction.

storyboard.claim: The ancestors' god Mars is described as the parent of tears, a foe to joy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow thinking on the red Mars horizon, an old belief in his head.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the old religion the clan rejects.
storyboard.addedInformation: The Mars horizon ties the old god to the planet itself.

storyboard.claim: Darrow's clan actively rejects the old god Mars.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow with an angry face in a dim cave, the rejection of the god shown in his stance.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the clan's rejection of the old religion, after the description of the god.
storyboard.addedInformation: The angry face shows the contempt for the old god, not a belief in it.

storyboard.claim: The clan rejects old gods but embraces the pioneer myth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow pointing toward the Mars horizon, choosing the pioneer story.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the rejection of old gods into the embrace of the new myth.
storyboard.addedInformation: The pointing gesture shows the choice of the pioneer story over the old religion.

storyboard.claim: The clan keeps believing the pioneer myth because of the sunk cost fallacy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow thinking, a neutral face in the cave.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the reason for choosing one myth over the other.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the fallacy the narration uses to explain the choice.

storyboard.claim: Believing the myth matters across generations, not only for one day.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow slumped, a sad face, in the cave.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Expands the sunk cost reason to the family line.
storyboard.addedInformation: The callout frames the stakes as generations, which the narration says it is.

storyboard.claim: If the terraforming myth is a lie, the dead of the mines died for nothing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A grave icon beside a sad Darrow in the cave, representing the dead miners.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the sunk cost into the cost of the dead.
storyboard.addedInformation: The grave is the dead family members; the callout makes the list concrete.

storyboard.claim: The human mind protects itself from the despair of meaningless death.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A shield beside an afraid, slumped Darrow in the cave.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the psychological reason for the belief in the grave beats.
storyboard.addedInformation: The shield reads as protection, the function the narration describes.

storyboard.claim: The alternative is that the miners are just disposable livestock for a cruel elite.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow, afraid and slumped, in the cave.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: States the alternative the myth prevents them from seeing.
storyboard.addedInformation: The fear on the face shows how unbearable the alternative is.

storyboard.claim: The myth is the cage: the clan must believe it just to survive the day.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Chains beside a worried Darrow in a medium shot in the cave.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Concludes the psychological argument of the previous beats.
storyboard.addedInformation: The chains read as bound, which is the cage the narration names.

storyboard.claim: People can only take so much pressure, so they need a release.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow in medium shot, a worried face in the dim cave.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the myth to the need for release.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the release the next beats describe.

storyboard.claim: The Golds allow the Reds some release, a gift of allowed joy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A gift icon beside Darrow talking in the township street.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the release from the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: The gift reads as something given, the allowance of joy the narration describes.

storyboard.claim: The Golds police the limits of joy to keep total control.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Dan, a Gold guard, stands over Darrow in a two-shot, watching.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the control the release is allowed under.
storyboard.addedInformation: The guard's threatening stance shows the policing of joy.

storyboard.claim: The Golds do not want silent drones; they let the Reds sing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow happy and celebrating in the street, singing.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrasts the allowed singing with what the Golds do not want.
storyboard.addedInformation: The strike rejects the drone image; the happy singing face shows the allowed joy.

storyboard.claim: The best dancers in the clan are the hell divers, because the drill work trains footwork.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow happy and dancing in the street.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the allowed joy into the dancing.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the dancing that the narration says the hell divers are skilled at.

storyboard.claim: The festivals, taverns and music let the Reds blow off steam.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow and Eo happily celebrating together in a two-shot in the tavern room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Lists the festivals and music that release the pressure.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the release the Golds allow, with Eo as a second face.

storyboard.claim: The Golds watch the dancing all night, but there is a very hard line.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A split: Dan smirking and watching on one side, Darrow happily dancing on the other.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Starts the forbidden line after the allowed dancing.
storyboard.addedInformation: The split divides the watcher from the dancer; the smirk shows the guard's control.

storyboard.claim: One dance is forbidden and is punished by immediate death.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A grave icon beside Dan, angry, pointing at the offender.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the penalty for crossing the hard line.
storyboard.addedInformation: The grave reads as death, the penalty the narration gives.

storyboard.claim: The forbidden dance is the foundational trauma for Darrow, because his father did it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow afraid in the cave, remembering the forbidden dance.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the penalty into Darrow's own family history.
storyboard.addedInformation: The afraid face shows the trauma the narration says it is.

storyboard.claim: The father did not rebel; he only danced, and was dragged to the center and hanged.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Dan grabbing a struggling Darrow in a two-shot in the township center.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the trauma with the arrest for the dance.
storyboard.addedInformation: The grabbing shows the dragging to the center; the callout rejects the idea of a rebellion.

storyboard.claim: The physics of Mars makes the hanging more horrible.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator speaking to the camera on a plain background.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns to the physical detail of the hanging that follows.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the next beat: the environment makes the death slow.
